Label: parvalbumin-positive basket cell of the hippocampus
Definition: A GABAergic inhibitory basket cell of the hippocampus that expresses parvalbumin. Its soma is located in the pyramidal cell layer of areas CA1, CA2, and CA3, or in the granule cell layer of the dentate gyrus. Its highly branched axon arborization is largely confined to the pyramidal or granule cell layer and forms basket-like perisomatic synapses on the soma and proximal dendrites of hundreds of principal neurons. It is fast-spiking and does not express cannabinoid receptor type 1 (Cnr1), distinguishing it from cholecystokinin-expressing basket cells. In rodents, it expresses the marker genes Pvalb, Gad1, and Gad2.
Exact synonym: PV basket cell|PV+ basket cell|parvalbumin basket cell
has soma location (DG granule cell layer: dentate gyrus granule cell layer [VALID - OLS4]
Comment: Evidence base is primarily from rodents (rat: Sik et al. 1995, PMID:7472426; mouse: Que et al. 2021, PMID:33398060; Whissell et al. 2015, PMID:26441554; Perrenoud et al. 2022, PMID:35802727; Bocchio et al. 2024, PMID:39401246). Parvalbumin basket cells have been described in human hippocampus and the term is not species-restricted. Soma location axioms for CA1 and CA3 pyramidal layers are HIGH confidence; the dentate gyrus granule cell layer axiom is MODERATE confidence (supported by PMID:35802727 and PMID:26441554 but basket cell identity of PV interneurons in this layer is less exhaustively characterised than in CA1). The Cnr1-negative annotation is biologically well-supported but a lacks_plasma_membrane_part axiom has not been added pending identification of an appropriate species-neutral PRO ID for cannabinoid receptor type 1.
